claims.claim: Reachability is exactly a sparse unary congruence-closure query.
claims.evidence: For each edge (o,X,t), impose f_X(t)=o. Congruence substitution gives exactly the stability rule t θ t' => o θ o' whenever both X-edges exist. Conversely, on θ-classes the partial assignment F_X([t])=[o] is well-defined by stability and can be extended arbitrarily to a total unary function, yielding a model that separates every pair outside θ; hence restricting the generated ground congruence to wires gives exactly θ. Independently, induction on well-nested push/pop walks shows that stack-neutral reachability is θ: nesting invokes the stability rule and concatenation invokes transitivity. Exit is therefore equivalent to the start wire sharing a θ-class with an outer-pin wire.
claims.witness: The algebra on θ-classes, with each well-defined partial F_X extended to a total function, is a separating model establishing the reverse congruence inclusion.
claims.search_method: Reconstructed the folding semantics, unary-equation model, and balanced-walk induction directly from the source; also tested closure computations on exhaustive finite dual graphs.

claims.claim: The congruence closure and exit query decompose exactly over weak components of the undirected support graph.
claims.evidence: Support-component equivalence is stable: two equivalent targets and both corresponding origins are connected through their incident support edges. Minimality therefore gives θ contained in the support components. Conversely, the disjoint union of the independently computed component closures is globally stable, so θ is contained in that union, while each local least closure is contained in the restriction of θ. Thus the two relations agree exactly, and no accepting wire outside the start component can answer the query.
claims.witness: The two minimality inclusions θ⊆⊔C θ_C and θ_C⊆θ|C establish equality component by component.
claims.search_method: Proved both inclusions from stability and leastness; exhaustively compared global and componentwise closures in the exact checker.

claims.claim: There is a deterministic O(W+B+E α(W+E)+E log(min{B,E}+1))-time, O(W+E+B)-space algorithm, sharpening the general sparse bound and eliminating dense W·B initialization.
claims.evidence: Each target-class map retains one edge per box. Every collision queues a stability-forced origin equality and permanently discards a distinct original edge, so at most E events occur. Inductively all unions are sound; when the queue empties, representatives of every pair of same-box edges with equivalent targets have collided, so the resulting partition is stable and hence equals the least closure. Counting/radix grouping costs O(W+B+E), and the DSU work costs O(E α(W+E)). For deterministic split/join tree melding, a merge of sizes m≤n costs O(m log(n/m+1)). With φ(s)=s log s, this is charged to the potential increase; deleting d duplicate keys adds only O(d log(K+1)), where K=min(B,E). Potential telescoping and at most E deletions give O(E log(K+1)). At most E map entries plus W DSU records and B-sized radix storage are retained.
claims.witness: The retained-edge invariant and the injective charging of every queued collision to its discarded original edge provide correctness, termination, and the event bound.
claims.search_method: Audited invariants and the potential calculation deductively; compared a literal sparse-map implementation against independent synchronous closure on 328,470 exhaustive graphs and 5,000 deterministic multigraph cases.

claims.claim: Both outcomes have certificates of size O(W+E) verifiable deterministically in O(W+E+B) time.
claims.evidence: For a no-instance, a W-entry partition P is verified stable by radix-grouping edges by (X,P(t)) and requiring a single P(o) per group; θ refines every such stable partition, so separation proves nonreachability. Taking P=θ proves completeness. For a yes-instance, record at most W−1 successful unions as a chronological binary forest. Each internal node supplies two same-box source edges and an earlier node containing both targets. Unique leaves, chronological children, edge identities, subtree membership, and an accepting root are all checkable in linear time using DFS intervals. Induction over internal nodes proves every subtree θ-equivalent, and any folding computation supplies the forest. Certificate storage is O(W+E), and radix sorting plus forest verification is O(W+E+B).
claims.witness: The checker constructs and independently verifies chronological merge forests, including prior target witnesses, and verifies the stable-partition condition on every tested graph.
claims.search_method: Proved soundness and completeness of both certificate forms and implemented exact set-based counterparts of the proposed linear verifiers.

claims.claim: The target O(W+E+B) bound holds for graded dual graphs: graphs admitting an integer rank ρ with ρ(o)=ρ(t)+1 for every edge (o,X,t).
claims.evidence: Induction on folding shows equivalences preserve rank. All edges originating at rank r have targets at rank r−1, whose classes are final before rank r is processed; consequently the final rank-r classes are precisely the ordinary connected components generated by groups sharing (X,class(t)). Stars represent those groups with O(E) total auxiliary edges. Difference constraints and normalized ranks are obtained in O(W+E); each component has rank span below W. Rank buckets, B- and W-sized timestamp arrays, and linear graph traversal process every wire and edge O(1) times, proving O(W+E+B) time and space.
claims.witness: Increasing-rank induction prevents any later or higher-rank fold from changing an already processed rank.
claims.search_method: Checked the rank induction, constraint construction, timestamp accounting, and star-connectivity implementation; exhaustively compared the graded algorithm with full closure.

claims.claim: On W-wire graded dual graphs, the exact maximum number of changing synchronous fixed-point rounds is floor((W−1)/2); this is attained with one box and E=2 floor((W−1)/2).
claims.evidence: A generator that first changes round k>1 must have targets that first became equivalent in round k−1; otherwise its origins would already have merged. Recursing to round one produces nontrivial equalities on k consecutive ranks, with two distinct wires on every equality rank and one common target on the rank below, so W≥2k+1. The stated construction uses z and pairs a_j,b_j, with both rank-one edges targeting z and each later pair targeting the preceding pair. Exactly one pair merges per round, giving R=floor((W−1)/2) rounds and 2R edges; an isolated wire handles even W.
claims.witness: Edges (a_0,X,z),(b_0,X,z) and, for j>0, (a_j,X,a_{j−1}),(b_j,X,b_{j−1}), with rank(a_j)=rank(b_j)=j+1.
claims.search_method: Proved the dependency-chain lower bound on required wires; exhaustively searched graded graphs through W=5 and checked the construction through W=12.

claims.claim: For unrestricted W-wire dual graphs, the universal maximum W−1 changing synchronous rounds is attained with one box, exactly E=W, origin outdegree one, and target indegree at most two.
claims.evidence: Every changing round strictly reduces the number of classes, giving the universal W−1 upper bound. For W≥2, the one-box edges (v_0,X,v_0), (v_1,X,v_0), and (v_i,X,v_{i−1}) for 2≤i<W merge precisely v_i into {v_0,…,v_{i−1}} during round i. Hence all W−1 rounds change. There are W edges, every origin has outdegree one, and only v_0 has target indegree two. Distinct pins realize all edges in the source model. For W=1, one self-loop realizes the stated parameters and zero rounds.
claims.witness: The self-loop-headed chain (v_0→v_0, v_1→v_0, v_i→v_{i−1}) under one box X.
claims.search_method: Verified the class-count upper bound and construction inductively; exhaustively searched unrestricted graphs through W=4 and checked constructed instances through W=12.

claims.claim: The exact minimum number of edges among W-wire instances attaining W−1 changing synchronous rounds is 0 when W=1 and W when W≥2.
claims.evidence: For W≥2, W−1 changing rounds reduce W singleton classes to one class. A wire that is not an edge origin can never be an endpoint of a generated nonreflexive equality and therefore remains singleton. Thus every wire must occur as an origin, forcing E≥W. The construction in claim 6 has exactly one edge from every wire and attains W−1 rounds, so the bound is tight. When W=1, the equality partition is already final, and the edgeless graph attains zero rounds, making zero minimal.
claims.witness: Lower bound: every final-class wire must occur among generator endpoints, hence among edge origins. Upper bound: the W-edge chain from claim 6; for W=1, the empty edge set.
claims.search_method: Proved the origin-coverage lower bound and checked exact minima exhaustively for all one-box graphs through W=4, including the W=1 boundary.

target_evidence: The draft does not prove the requested unrestricted O(W+E+B) decision bound. Its unrestricted algorithm retains inverse-Ackermann and logarithmic terms, while its linear algorithm applies only to graded dual graphs. The congruence formulation, component reduction, certificate results, graded algorithm, and extremal-round theorems are nevertheless correct material progress. The explicit claimed resolution PARTIAL is therefore accurate and not overstated.
